{{Wireless adapter |brand=Qualcomm |model=65-VE239-P2 |revision= |upc= |ean= |asin= |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=10/18/2007 |manuf_country= |is_manuf=No |manuf= |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |availability=unreleased |if=Mini PCIe |if_bus_version= |if_connector_type= |form_factor= |vendor_id= |device_id= |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |id_string= |fcc_id=J9C-65VE239P2 |ic_id=2723A-65VE239P2 |chip1_brand=Qualcomm |chip1_model=WFB4130;WFB4130, B0841.00, C5734004, WAFER#03; |chip2_brand=Qualcomm |chip2_model= |chip3_brand= |chip3_model= |chip4_brand= |chip4_model= |addl_chips= |accessible_UART=No |flags= |ant_conn=U.FL |802dot11_protocols=abgn |txchains=2 |rxchains=3 |sstreams=2 |oui=00:0A:F5 |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} This device (alternate model '''''MC423D_H'''''?) uses '''Qualcomm''''s WFB400 chipset (the successor to '''Airgo''''s AGN300 chipset). It was likely never publicly released.
"701-00224-04" is silkscreened on the board in the FCC photos.
The Windows device description shown in the FCC manual is shown as <small>'''QUALCOMM WFB400 802.11n Wireless Adapter'''</small> and <small>'''Airgo Networks AGN400 True MIMO (tm) Wireless Adapter'''</small>.
A MAC label w/ a 00:0A:F5 ('''Airgo''') OUI is affixed to the device in the FCC photos. It has been assigned to this entry for no reason.
